newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH ENTREPENEURS SEE BETTER TIMES AHEAD - SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH ENTREPENEURS SEE BETTER TIMES AHEAD - SURVEY.

text.p: The outlook for small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) has improved since spring and a majority now expects better times, the Finnish Entrepeneurs said in a statement on Monday.
In the association's latest cyclical barometer, 24 percent expected the business cycle to improve while 11.5 percent expected it to deteriorate, it said.
In the previous survey last spring, 18 percent saw worse times and only 15 percent an improvement.
"Companies' net sales and profitability will improve significanly further," it said.
"The outlook for services and trade is somewhat better than for construction and industry," the association said.
However, employment in SMEs would not see any major improvement and the service sector was the only one that planned to take on new personnel, it said.
The main problems for SMEs were unhealthy competition and high indirect labour costs.
